panels.title: P90 Peer Latency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*90th-percentile round-trip latency to connected peers, in milliseconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the p90 peer latency.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; green under 200ms, yellow to 500ms, red above.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under 200ms.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising latency, which points to network congestion or geographically distant, poorly performing peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerQualityGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#peer)

panels.title: Insane/Diverged Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Count of connected peers whose ledger state has diverged from the network.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the diverged-peer count.*

###### Reading it:
*Zero is healthy; any count means those peers disagree on ledger state.*

###### Healthy range:
*0 diverged peers.*

###### Watch for:
*A persistent non-zero count, which can indicate peers on a fork or misbehaving peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Insane / diverged peers** *(per node)* — connected peers whose ledger state disagrees with the network — possibly on a fork or misbehaving.
- **Fork** *(network-wide)* — when nodes validate divergent ledger chains instead of a single agreed history.

###### Computation boundary:

panels.title: Inbound vs Outbound Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Active inbound versus outbound peer connection counts.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of active inbound and outbound peer counts.*

###### Reading it:
*A balanced mix is healthy for connectivity and resilience.*

###### Healthy range:
*A mix of both; some outbound connections present.*

###### Watch for:

###### Keywords:

panels.title: Resource Disconnects
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Cumulative count of peers dropped for exceeding resource (load) limits.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the resource-disconnect total over time.*

###### Reading it:
*A flat line is healthy; a rising line means peers are being dropped for overuse.*

###### Healthy range:
*Flat / near constant.*

###### Watch for:
*A steep climb, which flags aggressive or misbehaving peers being shed as backpressure.*

###### Keywords:
- **Resource disconnect** *(per node)* — a peer dropped for exceeding resource/load limits — the node shedding abusive or overactive peers.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerServerInfoGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#resource-disconnect)

panels.title: Peer Disconnect Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Per-second rate at which this node closes peer connections, across all reasons.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the peer-disconnect counter over the selected rate interval, summed per node. Narrow it with the Disconnect Reason and Disconnect Direction variables.*

###### Reading it:
*A low, steady rate is ordinary churn. The height of the line says how fast the peer set is turning over, not why — pair it with Peer Disconnects By Reason & Direction for the cause.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low and steady relative to each node's own baseline.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained rise, which means the peer set is churning faster than it is being replaced and can leave the node short of peers to sync from. Distinct from Resource Disconnects, which counts only the resource-charge subset and carries no reason breakdown.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer disconnect** *(per node)* — a peer connection closed by this node, for any reason, counted once per teardown.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::close`

###### References:
[Resource disconnect](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#resource-disconnect)

panels.title: Peer Disconnects By Reason & Direction
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Peer closes over time, split by why they closed and by which side opened the connection.*

###### How it's computed:
*Increase in the peer-disconnect counter per rate interval, grouped by node, reason and direction. Filter with the Disconnect Reason and Disconnect Direction variables.*

###### Reading it:
*The split separates our-fault backpressure from topology and network faults. large_sendq and charge_resources are this node shedding a peer it cannot keep up with. not_useful and ping_timeout are topology and liveness. read_error and write_error are the transport. graceful, stopping and shutdown are ordinary lifecycle, not faults.*

###### Healthy range:
*Mostly graceful; the fault reasons near zero.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained large_sendq or charge_resources means this node is the bottleneck and is dropping the very peers it needs to sync from, so a slow node makes itself slower. A rising not_useful or ping_timeout on outbound points at the peer set instead. This is the time-shaped view of the split; the Ledger Sync Health dashboard carries the same split as a window total.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer disconnect reason** *(per node)* — the cause recorded when a peer connection is closed, paired with whether that connection was inbound or outbound.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::close`

###### References:
[Resource disconnect](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#resource-disconnect) · [Insane / diverged peers](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#insane-diverged-peers)

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_join(sum by (reason, direction, service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_work_item) (increase(peer_disconnect_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", reason=~"$disconnect_reason", direction=~"$disconnect_direction"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", " ", "reason", "direction"), "xrpl_ident", ", ", "service_instance_id", "xrpl_branch", "xrpl_work_item"), "xrpl_ident", "[$1]", "xrpl_ident", "(?:, )*(.*[^, ])(?:, )*")
